title: A Computation of the Expected Number of Posts in a Finite Random Graph Order
locators: Sec. 2, Theorem 2.1 and Eqs. (1)–(2); Sec. 3, Theorem 3.1 and Eqs. (3)–(4).
relevance: Direct classical probabilistic predecessor for the Euler-product post-tail factor. For real 0<p<1 computes the probability that a fixed element is related to every later element as κ(q)=∏_{j≥1}(1−q^j), and the probability it is a post as λ_{k−1}(q)κ(q). Does not provide a complex covariant measure or the common-factor prescription for all principal H.
limits: Full text read at cited sections; conclusions are for real probability parameters in random graph orders, not complex measures. No broader priority or dependency audit.
version: arXiv:0809.2258v2; arXiv version history last revised 2008-09-25.
assumptions: Random graph order/transitive percolation with real probability p in (0,1), q=1−p; independent link choices with transitive closure.
conclusion: The future-descendant condition contributes the Euler product κ(q); independence from the preceding-ancestor condition gives Pr(k is post)=λ_{k−1}(q)κ(q), approaching κ(q)^2 for large k.
proof_status: Theorem 2.1 and proof read in full; the finite expected-number result in Sec. 3 also screened.
dependencies: Random graph order probability model and Euler function partial products; cited prior result of Alon et al. for infinitely many posts, not independently audited.
open_questions: No complex-parameter continuation or covariant finite complex-measure statement was found in the screened paper.
